system.biography:
A typical lillend’s coils are 20 feet long. The creature weighs about 3,800 pounds. A few lillends have male torsos.

Lillends speak Celestial, Infernal, Abyssal, and Common.

Combat

Lillends are generally peaceful unless they intend vengeance against someone they believe guilty of harming, or even threatening, a favored art form, artwork, or artist. Then they become implacable foes. They use their spells and spell-like abilities to confuse and weaken opponents before entering combat. A covey of lillends usually discusses strategy before a battle.

A lillend’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and good-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Constrict (Ex)

A lillend deals 2d6+5 points of damage with a successful grapple check. Constricting uses the entire lower portion of its body, so it cannot take any move actions when constricting, though it can still attack with its sword.

Improved Grab (Ex)

To use this ability, a lillend must hit with its tail slap attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict.

Spells

A lillend casts arcane spells as a 6th-level bard.

Typical Bard Spells Known (3/4/3; save DC 14 + spell level)

0— dancing lights, daze, detect magic, lullaby, mage hand, read magic; 1st— charm person, cure light wounds, identify, sleep; 2nd—hold person, invisibility, sound burst.

Spell-Like Abilities

3/day—darkness, hallucinatory terrain (DC 18), knock, light; 1/day—charm person (DC 15), speak with animals, speak with plants. Caster level 10th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

A lillend also has the bardic music ability as a 6th-level bard.

Skills

Lillends have a +4 racial bonus on Survival checks.

system.description: You are adept at casting spells in melee.
system.benefit: You get a +4 bonus on Concentration checks made to cast a spell or use a spell-like ability while on the defensive or while you are grappling or pinned.

system.description: You can cast spells that last longer than normal.
system.benefit: An extended spell lasts twice as long as normal. A spell with a duration of concentration, instantaneous, or permanent is not affected by this feat. An extended spell uses up a spell slot one level higher than the spell's actual level.
You get a +2 bonus on all Reflex saving throws.

system.description: You can evaluate the monetary value of an object.
Make a Concentration check whenever you might be distracted (by taking damage, by harsh weather, and so on) while engaged in some action that requires your full attention.
You can use this skill to persuade others to agree with your arguments, to resolve differences, and to gather valuable information or rumors from people.
Ancient mysteries, magic traditions, arcane symbols, cryptic phrases, constructs, dragons, magical beasts. Like other Knowledge skills, each Knowledge field is a separate skill with its own ranks.
Your Listen check is either made against a DC that reflects how quiet the noise is that you might hear, or it is opposed by the target's Move Silently check.
You can get a hunch about a social situation or read a person.
You are skilled at working with magic and can identify spells as they are cast or spells already in place.
Your Spot check is either made against a DC that reflects how obvious the object is, or it is opposed by the target's Hide check.
You are skilled at surviving in the wild and at following tracks.

What it does (SRD): On a successful grapple check, the creature deals extra bludgeoning damage (the amount is given in the creature’s stat block). Constrict usually requires a successful grapple after a grab-capable attack.

ThirdEra: Leave Mechanical effects and Capability grants empty here; enter the printed constriction damage and any special rules in the NPC’s Description or natural attack notes so it matches the SRD stat block.

What it does (SRD): If the creature hits with a listed natural weapon, it can attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking attacks of opportunity. Details (size modifiers, opposed checks, holding vs pinning) follow the grapple rules.

ThirdEra: This template has no numeric rows in Mechanical effects or Capability grants. Track grapple state in play; use the NPC’s natural attacks and CMB/CMD from the sheet when resolving the grapple.

Constrict (Ex): Deals listed constriction damage on a successful grapple check; uses the entire lower body — cannot take move actions while constricting but may still attack with its sword.

Spells: Casts arcane spells as a 6th-level bard (typical spells known and slots per stat block).

Spell-like abilities: 3/day — darkness, hallucinatory terrain (DC 18), knock, light; 1/day — charm person (DC 15), speak with animals, speak with plants. Caster level 10th; save DCs Charisma-based.

Bardic music: As a 6th-level bard.

Weapons (Ex): Natural and wielded weapons are chaotic and good for overcoming DR.

Skills: +4 racial on Survival.

What it does (SRD): The creature ignores the first N points of damage from each attack or effect of the listed energy type.

ThirdEra: Type and amount are set under CGS parameters and overrides.

What it does (SRD): The creature is immune to poison: it does not take ability damage or hit point damage from poison, and it ignores other harmful poison effects unless a specific effect overrides immunity.

ThirdEra: On this item’s Details tab, poison immunity is under Capability grants (immunity), not as save or AC bonuses in Mechanical effects. The character sheet lists it with other immunities and defenses from the creature’s items and features.
